content.title: About
content.content: Peanuts, dry roasted, salted are whole peanuts that have been roasted without added oil and lightly salted. The dry‑roasting process gives them a crunchy texture and a rich, nutty aroma, while a touch of salt enhances the flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts.
Dry roasting without oil preserves more nutrients compared with oil‑fried peanuts.
Salt is usually added after roasting to keep the nuts crisp.
Peanuts are a staple in many world cuisines, from Asian sauces to African stews and American snacks.
Dry roasted peanuts are the base for peanut butter, confectionery, and trail mixes.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Peanuts provide about 25 % protein, making them a valuable plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats
items.content: These fats support heart health and help absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peanuts contain niacin, thiamine, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: magnesium, phosphorus, potassium
items.content: These minerals aid muscle function, nerve signaling, and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Resveratrol and other phenolic compounds in peanuts help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common food allergens and can cause severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because they are energy‑dense, portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The salted version may be unsuitable for people with hypertension or kidney disease.

items.title: Aflatoxins
items.content: Improper storage can allow mold growth that produces aflatoxins, so proper storage conditions are essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dry roasted salted peanuts are perfect as a snack on their own, tossed into salads, added to Asian dishes, mixed into granola or trail‑mixes, or used as a crunchy topping for soups and desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life store in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
